claim: Every autonomy failure this session was a HARNESS defect, not a model one.

runs.blocker: --model was advertised by the CLI and never reached the worker; controller read HCLI_MODEL_PATH which nothing set

runs.reached: worker + model calls + a written test file
runs.blocker: insert/append fragments compiled STANDALONE and falsely rejected as 'unexpected indent at line 1' -- the same false rejection already fixed for op=replace, never extended to the splicing family. The model was holding a correct guard and was told it had made a syntax error it had not made.
runs.fixed: splicing ops rebuild the resulting file from their anchor and judge THAT

runs.blocker: every test command came back as the bare string NOT_ADMITTED, which names no accepted form, so the model alternated between two rejected shapes forever
runs.fixed: the refusal now names the three accepted forms

runs.reached: a test command ADMITTED and EXECUTED, rc=1 -- a genuine RED
runs.blocker: not yet isolated; the unit still did not reach an accepted terminal

hcli_owned: 0 of 25, unchanged. The bar is an ACCEPTED unit and none was reached.
what_the_model_actually_did_well: took its goal from disk with no human typing one
decomposed a four-step instruction into its own obligations
wrote a correct, well-formed pytest with a fixture and pytest.raises
found an accepted test-command form once the refusal named one
had the RIGHT fix for a real path traversal, and lost it to a false rejection
honest_reading: The campaign's story was 'HCLI cannot carry a unit'. The measured story is that three harness defects stood between it and a terminal, each one making a correct action look like a model error. Two are fixed and demonstrated; the third moved the failure one stage later. That is not autonomy achieved, but it is a different diagnosis than the one this session started with.
